'''Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine''' (Takakuramusubimiko-jinja) is a shrine located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}} {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|qid=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}} {{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|en|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|qid=Q1355625|lt=Atsuta Ward}} {{ill|Takakura-chō|ja|高蔵町 (名古屋市)|lt=Takakura-cho|lt_ja=高蔵町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakura-cho (Nagoya)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q56449178}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myoujindai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9610964}}) and a Keigai-Sessha of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|en|Atsuta Shrine|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine}}.

Like Atsuta Shrine, it enshrines the ancestral deity of Owari. Serving as the guardian and tutelary deity of the Takakura area, it is deeply revered locally and affectionately called “Takakura-sama.”

== Worshipped deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}}
The enshrined deity is the following one figure<ref name="HistoryDocument">Shrine History Document.</ref>:
* '''{{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|qid=Q11668757|lt=Takakura-shita-no-mikoto}}''' (Takakura-shita-no-mikoto)

== History ==
=== Founding ===
The founding is unknown. According to tradition, it may date to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|ja|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q335181}} (673–686)<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>, or it is said to have been established around the same time as the main shrine of Atsuta Shrine{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

Regarding the Keigai-Sessha of Atsuta Shrine—including Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine—there is a theory correlating its origins with the distribution of various Owari powers during the Kofun period<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488"/>. In this context, it is speculated that the dominant forces on the Atsuta plateau (such as {{ill|Danpusan Kofun|en|Danpusan Kofun|qid=Q5221001|lt=Danpusan Kofun}}, {{ill|Shiratori Kofun (Nagoya)|ja|白鳥古墳 (名古屋市)|lt=Hakuchou Kofun|lt_ja=白鳥古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakuchou Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580543}}, and {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|en|Atsuta Shrine|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine}}) absorbed other powers, resulting in the incorporation of various shrines into Atsuta Shrine’s divine genealogy<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488">Shinshu Nagoya City History, Volume 1, Nagoya City, 1997, pp. 486–488.</ref>.

=== General History ===
According to the national histories ({{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=National Histories}}), the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}} in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|en|Jōwa (Heian period)|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} (836) contains a passage listing three deities of Atsuta Shrine—the Hiwari-mikogami, Mago-waka-mikogami, and the deity of Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Atsuta Ōkami Mikogami) – among the renowned deities{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

In the {{ill|Enchō|en|Enchō|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5th year (927) version of the ''Engishiki'' ({{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}), in Owari Province’s {{ill|Aichi District|en|Aichi District|qid=Q552687|lt=Aichi District}}, it is recorded as “Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine Myoujindai” and is listed alongside the {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myoujindai Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9610964}}{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}. Moreover, in the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Kokunai Shinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11041830}}, it is recorded either as “Takakura Myōjin” or “Takakura Myōjin”{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

During the construction in the {{ill|Genki (era)|en|Genki (era)|qid=Q1145064|lt=Genki era}} 2nd year (1571), there was a donation from {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}; in the Edo period, in the {{ill|Genna|de|Genna (Ära)|es|Genna|fa|گننا|fr|Ère Genna|id|Genna|it|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|ko|겐나|ru|Гэнна|simple|Genna|sr|Гена|sv|Genna|tr|Genna|zh|元和 (日本)|qid=Q635245|lt=Genwa}} 4th year (1618), repairs were carried out by {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|en|Hachisuka Iemasa|qid=Q1073557|lt=Hachisuka Iemasa}}, and in the {{ill|Jōkyō|en|Jōkyō|qid=Q1146221|lt=Jōkyō era}} 3rd year (1686), when Atsuta Shrine was reconstructed by the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|Tokugawa shogunate}}, similar repairs were made to this shrine{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

The shrine building, originally in the {{ill|Owari-zukuri|ja|尾張造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari-zukuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11465322}} style with a vermilion finish, was almost entirely destroyed by wartime damage in the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}} 20th year (1945) and was rebuilt in a form approximating its pre-war appearance in the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}} 38th year (1963){{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

=== Divine Rank ===
* Record of the conferral of divine Rank during the {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=National Histories}} period:
** On December 12, in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|en|Jōwa (Heian period)|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} (836), it was listed among the renowned deities (as recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}}) – noted as “Takakurayui Mikoshi.”
* After the era of the National Histories:
** Either Senior Second Rank<ref>[{{NDLDC|991014/413}} ''Shinja Kakoroku, Volume 1'' (Imperial Studies Institute, 1902, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 413 lines]</ref>, or Upper Senior Second Rank<ref>{{PDFlink|[https://websv.aichi-pref-library.jp/wahon/pdf/1103283156-001.pdf ''Domestic Shinmyōchō'']]} (Bunsei 13 [1830] transcribed combined edition, Aichi Prefectural Library “Precious Wa Books Digital Library”) 6 lines.</ref>, or Junior Second Rank{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}} (in the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Kokunai Shinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11041830}}) – the inscription being “Takakura Myōjin” or “Takakura Myōjin”{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}. Note that the Ranking varies among manuscripts.

== Subordinate Shrines ==
Within the precincts, the following four subsidiary shrines are enshrined<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>. In the early modern period, it is said that there were also the {{ill|Mitarai Shrine|ja|御手洗神社}} and the {{ill|Watatsumi Shrine (disambiguation)|en|Watatsumi Shrine|qid=Q123530063|lt=Kaijin Shrine}}.
* {{ill|Hokotori Shrine|ja|鉾取社}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Hokotori-no-Kami|ja|鉾取神}}
* {{ill|Shingu Shrine|ja|新宮社}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo}}
* {{ill|Mii Shrine|ja|御井社}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kimata-no-Kami|ja|御井神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mii-no-Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 木俣神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11092833}}
* {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q514480}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama}}
*: It is said that the mother of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} (later known as {{ill|Ōmandokoro|en|Ōmandokoro|qid=Q5353737|lt=Ōmandokoro}}) once took the young Hideyoshi with her to pray for his rise in life, which is why this shrine is also known by the alternate name “Taikō Shusse Inari.”

== Festivals ==
* Inari Shrine Festival (on Hatsu-uma day)
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Spring Grand Festival (old Hatsu-uma day)
* Child Custody Festival (April 3)
*: A custom in which young children are entrusted to the enshrined deity until the age of 15, praying for healthy growth and protection from pests, with a subsequent thanksgiving visit once safely grown.
* Annual Festival (June 1)
* Mii Festival (on Doyō-iri day)
*: It is believed that if a child peers into the well of Mii Shrine on this day, it brings benefits of pest protection<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>.
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Autumn Grand Festival (November 8)
